method: Rebuild from primary text. Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code §§675, 1086, 1088, 1088.5 and 1735 were fetched from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov and read. The construing case was located through CourtListener. Assertions describe the REBUILT body.
queries: Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code §1086, §1088, §1088.5 full text (leginfo)
Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code §675, §1735 full text (leginfo)

assertions.text: registration is due within 15 days after becoming an employer
assertions.note: §1086(a), verbatim. Note what the clock runs from: becoming an employer 'as defined in this part', not paying $100.

assertions.text: 'employer' means an employing unit that, in the current or preceding calendar year, has one or more employees and pays wages in excess of $100 in any calendar quarter
assertions.note: §675, verbatim. The $100 threshold the previous clause attributed to §1086 is here, and it comes with a current-or-preceding-calendar-year test the previous body did not have. The previous body also said 'more than one hundred dollars ($100)', which matches 'in excess of'.

assertions.text: the employer files a report of contributions, a quarterly return and a report of wages
since January 1, 2018 all employers must file electronically, subject to an approved waiver
assertions.note: §1088(h)(2)-(3), verbatim: 'effective January 1, 2018, all employers shall file the report of contributions, quarterly return, and report of wages electronically', with a waiver available for lack of automation, severe economic hardship, a current federal exemption or other good cause, valid for a year or longer at the Director's discretion. The previous body said to file 'on the assigned schedule' without saying the channel is mandatory — a defect its own list had recorded.

assertions.text: new hires must be reported within 20 days, and so must a returning employee separated for at least 60 consecutive days
assertions.note: §1088.5(b) and (d)(1). The 60-day rehire rule was absent from the previous body and from its defect list. §1088.5(d)(2) sets the alternative for electronic transmitters: two monthly transmissions not less than 12 and not more than 16 days apart.

assertions.text: personal liability under §1735 requires a WILFUL failure and attaches to an officer, major stockholder or other person having charge of the affairs of a corporate, association, LLP or LLC employing unit
assertions.note: §1735, verbatim, quoted in full by the Bankruptcy Appellate Panel in In re Hansen. The previous body said 'Unremitted withholding can be assessed personally against responsible individuals' — no wilfulness, no defined class, and it left out that contributions as well as withholdings are covered.

priorDefects: citation-gap: the clause cited only §1086 while asserting the $100 threshold (§675), the return-filing duty (§1088) and personal liability (§1735).
omitted: mandatory electronic filing since January 1, 2018 (§1088(h)).
omitted: the new hire reporting duty entirely, and the 60-day rehire rule (§1088.5).
omitted: 'wilfully' from the personal liability rule, and the statutory class of persons it reaches (§1735).
omitted: that §1735 covers contributions as well as withholdings.
omitted: the current-or-preceding-calendar-year element of the definition of employer (§675).
gaps: The withholding deposit schedule is set by Unemp. Ins. Code §13021, which was not read. The clause says 'on the assigned schedule', which is accurate and empty.

The DE 9 and DE 9C form numbers were removed from the body because §1088 describes reports and returns without naming forms. The form numbers may well be right, but edd.ca.gov was not opened for this rebuild and the corpus should not carry form numbers nobody has checked against the agency.
emp_ca_registration is a near-duplicate of this clause, is unsourced, and was not rebuilt here. The two will now disagree.
Penalties for late registration or late returns were not researched.

judicialQuotations.quote: Any officer, major stockholder, or other person, having charge of the affairs of a corporate, association, registered limited liability partnership or foreign limited liability partnership, or limited liability company employing unit, who willfully fails to pay contributions required by this division or withholdings required by Div...

singleOpinionCaveat: In re Hansen is a federal bankruptcy appellate decision applying §1735 as background to a dischargeability question, not a California court construing it. It is cited only because it reproduces the statutory text and shows the section in operation — the EDD there assessed an individual for $4.8 million. The quotation is truncated in the source excerpt at 'required by Div...' and should be re-read in full before it is quoted where a reader will rely on it. The rebuild rests on the statute.
